sections.title: ML Specialty Prereq: the machine learning AIP-C01 takes for granted

keyTerms.definition: The AWS managed platform for building, training, and deploying machine learning models.
AWS Certified AI Practitioner, the exam that taught the AI vocabulary this volume builds on.

recall.question: What does this volume teach that the AIF-C01 volume did not?
recall.answer: The machinery: getting data ready, training on SageMaker, tuning, evaluating, deploying, and keeping models healthy.

keyTerms.definition: AWS Certified Machine Learning Engineer - Associate, the live exam that replaced MLS-C01.
The retired AWS Certified Machine Learning Specialty exam.
Scoring where strength in one domain offsets weakness in another; no per-domain minimum.

recall.question: How many questions does MLA-C01 have, and how many count?
recall.answer: 65 total: 50 scored and 15 unscored, and you cannot tell which is which.

recall.question: What does the 720 compensatory pass mark mean in practice?
recall.answer: You can be weak in one domain if you are strong in another; no single domain can fail you alone.

keyTerms.definition: The exit test at each rung; the 4-hour rung only counts if you do each one.
The compressed trees at the end: algorithm picker, endpoint picker, and drift response.

recall.question: What are the three study rungs and their exit tests?
recall.answer: 30 minutes: read the exam summary and the three decision trees. 4 hours: read one domain at a time and do each knowledge check. 1 day: do all 20 practice questions.

keyTerms.definition: Amazon's object storage; the center of every ML data story on AWS.
The service that moves files from on-premises or another cloud into S3.
The service that carries live event streams into the pipeline.
A columnar format that stores each column together; the exam's default for training data.
One class dominating the data, like 1% fraud versus 99% normal.
The managed service for human data labeling with private, vendor, or public workforces.

recall.question: Nightly CSV dumps arrive on-premises and a no-code analyst must clean them weekly. Which two services?
recall.answer: DataSync moves the files into S3, and DataBrew is the no-code cleaning tool for analysts.

recall.question: Why is 99% accuracy meaningless on a 1% fraud dataset, and what are the three fixes?
recall.answer: The always-say-normal model scores 99% and catches zero fraud. Fix the data with resampling or SMOTE, fix the model with class weights, or fix the yardstick with precision-recall or AUC-PR.

recall.question: A 1 TB orders table serves one-month queries. How does monthly partitioning cut the Athena bill?
recall.answer: The query scans about 85 GB instead of 1 TB, so at $5 per TB scanned the cost drops from $5.00 to about $0.42.

keyTerms.definition: Turning raw data into columns the model can learn from; the highest-payoff pipeline step.
One binary column per value; fits categories with few values.
Dense vector representations used when a category has thousands of values.
SageMaker's shared home for features, with an online store and an offline store.
Training on feature values as they were at event time, never as they are today.
Building features from future data the model will not have at prediction time.

recall.question: A model one-hots zip code with 12,000 values and training crawls. What is the fix?
recall.answer: Replace one-hot with embeddings, the hashing trick, or target encoding; 12,000 sparse columns are slow and noisy.

recall.question: Why must training features be point-in-time correct?
recall.answer: Using today's values for last year's events smuggles the future into training; the model sees numbers it will not have at prediction time.

recall.question: Two teams compute the same feature twice and the copies drift apart. Which service fixes this?
recall.answer: SageMaker Feature Store: ingest once, serve training from the offline store and real-time inference from the online store.

keyTerms.definition: The default SageMaker algorithm for tabular classification and regression.
Training on spare EC2 capacity at up to 90% off, with two minutes of interruption notice.
Saving training progress to S3 so an interrupted spot job resumes instead of restarting.
Distributed training where each GPU holds a full model copy and trains on a different data slice.
Settings fixed before training starts: learning rate, batch size, trees, epochs.
Tuning that learns from past trials; the SageMaker automatic tuning default.

recall.question: Predict churn from a customer table with labels present. Which built-in algorithm does the exam expect?
recall.answer: XGBoost: tabular rows and columns with labels is its home turf.

recall.question: A training job must finish cheaply and can tolerate interruptions. Which setup fits?
recall.answer: Managed Spot Training with S3 checkpointing: up to 90% off, and the job resumes after interruption instead of restarting.

recall.question: A tuning job should explore efficiently and learn from earlier trials. Which strategy?
recall.answer: Bayesian optimization: it builds a model of past trial results and picks the next combination smartly.

keyTerms.definition: TP divided by TP plus FP: of all alarms raised, how many were real.
TP divided by TP plus FN: of all real positives, how many were caught.
The harmonic mean of precision and recall; it punishes gaming one side.
Training error tiny but validation error much bigger; the model memorized noise.
Both training and validation errors big; the model never learned the pattern.
Rotating the validation slice and averaging scores for a stable performance estimate.

recall.question: Fraud model scores TP=8, FP=5, FN=2, TN=85. What are precision and recall?
recall.answer: Precision is 8 divided by 13, about 0.62. Recall is 8 divided by 10, or 0.80.

recall.question: A model trains to 98% accuracy but validates at 72%. What is wrong, and which two actions help?
recall.answer: Overfitting: the train-validation gap is the diagnosis. Add regularization with early stopping, or collect more training data.

recall.question: Missing a tumor is worse than a false alarm. Which metric guides tuning?
recall.answer: Recall: the cost of a false negative dwarfs the cost of a false positive.

sections.title: Domain 2 continued · The SageMaker workflow tools

keyTerms.definition: SageMaker Experiments: logs every training run with hyperparameters, metrics, data, and code version.
Versions winning models and gates promotion until a human approves.
Scans data for bias before training and predictions for bias after; explains with SHAP.
SageMaker Debugger: hooks into live training jobs with built-in rules for vanishing gradients, overfitting, and stalled loss.

recall.question: A bank must prove its loan model does not discriminate and explain rejections. Which tool, and when does it run?
recall.answer: SageMaker Clarify. Before training it measures bias in the data; after training it measures bias in predictions and explains individual decisions with SHAP.

recall.question: How does a registered model version reach production?
recall.answer: It registers as PendingManualApproval, and nothing deploys until a human flips the status to Approved.

sections.title: Domain 3 · Deployment and orchestration of ML workflows (22%)

keyTerms.definition: An always-warm endpoint answering in milliseconds; you pay for every hour it runs.
Scales from zero with pay per request; watch cold starts against latency budgets.
Scheduled scoring of a full S3 dataset with no endpoint; cheapest per prediction.
Two model versions behind one endpoint with traffic split by weight, for A/B tests.
The retraining workflow as code: a DAG of steps triggered by schedule or S3 events.
An endpoint guardrail that swaps the whole fleet to the new version at once.

recall.question: 50 million product images are scored nightly at 2 AM in one burst and nobody waits. Cheapest option?
recall.answer: Batch transform: it starts for the job, scores the S3 dataset, and shuts down.

recall.question: Validate a new model on 10% of live traffic with instant rollback. Which approach?
recall.answer: Production variants on the existing endpoint: add the model as a second variant with weight 0.1, and rollback is one weight update.

recall.question: Which combination gives automated retraining on new data with human approval before production?
recall.answer: SageMaker Pipelines triggered by S3 events, plus Model Registry approval gates before deploy.

keyTerms.definition: The inputs change shape while the model keeps running on data it barely knows.
The world changes meaning while the inputs look the same.
Fairness across groups erodes over time in production.
Captures a baseline from training data, then hourly live traffic into S3, and alarms on violations.
The training-job setting that blocks all internet access.
Execution roles that read their input bucket and write their output bucket, nothing more.

recall.question: Accuracy is falling but input feature distributions look unchanged. What drift is this, and what does the fix need?
recall.answer: Concept drift: the world changed, not the inputs. Retraining needs fresh labeled data from the new world.

recall.question: Training must have no internet, company-key encryption on volumes, and private S3 without NAT. Which settings?
recall.answer: Network isolation on the training job, a gateway VPC endpoint for S3, and a KMS key on the volumes.

recall.question: A CloudWatch alarm on violations should retrain only after human review. Which pieces?
recall.answer: The alarm fires Lambda, Lambda starts a SageMaker Pipeline, and the registry approval gate sits before deploy.

sections.title: The whole exam on one page

keyTerms.definition: The exam's most repeated traps, each separated by one crisp difference.
Reusing a previous tuning job to speed up the next hyperparameter search.
The tuning search that learns from past trials; the SageMaker default.
One endpoint hosting many models on the same container, loading each on demand.

recall.question: A hospital needs real-time tumor predictions, misses are unacceptable, traffic is steady. Which two choices?
recall.answer: A real-time endpoint and optimize for recall: steady live traffic needs always-on serving, and the cost of a miss dominates.

recall.question: The registry shows v7 PendingManualApproval and v6 approved and deployed; a drift alarm fires. What happens?
recall.answer: The pipeline retrains, registers v8 as pending, and a human approves before anything deploys.
